title: When a model memorises instead of learning

probes.question: What does an overfitted model do?
options: Follows its training data too closely and may fail on new data

probes.question: True or false: overfitting means a model has learned to generalise well to new data.

image.alt: A plot with a few data points, a straight black line, and a wiggly red curve that passes through every point then shoots upward.

body.claim: A model can fit its training data so closely that it gets worse on new data.
body.why: This is overfitting. The model starts to memorise the training data instead of learning the underlying trend, partly by treating noise as if it were structure. It then has a higher error rate on unseen data.
